title: Dynamical Masses for 23 Pre-main-sequence Stars in Upper Scorpius: A Critical Test of Stellar Evolutionary Models
question: Do pre-main-sequence evolutionary models reproduce Keplerian dynamical masses of K/M stars in Upper Sco (5-11 Myr), and does using dynamical instead of isochronal masses change the dust mass vs stellar mass slope?

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the ALMA data
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA; pipeline continuum images used; line cubes resampled to 0.4 km/s with cvel2 and imaged with tclean (Briggs, robust 0.5 for most sources, multiscale and robust 0.0-1.0 for extended sources)

recipe.goal: Detect lines and continuum and characterise morphology
recipe.method: CO detection = >5 sigma in at least two consecutive channels; continuum detection at 3 sigma; 2D Gaussian imfit to moment 0 and continuum images; compare continuum and CO position angles to test for outflow contamination
assumptions: ~90 degree misalignment of continuum and CO major axes is the outflow signature

recipe.goal: Derive stellar luminosities from SED fits
recipe.method: Fit optical-infrared photometry to BT-Settl models over a grid in A_V and theta=R*/d with Gaia distances; L* from integrated best-fit SED
key_parameters: log(g) 3.0-4.5; A_V 0 to 4.5 in steps of 0.1
assumptions: Solar metallicity, no alpha enhancement; extinction law of Wang & Chen 2019; extra 10% flux uncertainty for variability

recipe.goal: Fit Keplerian disk models to the CO visibilities with MCMC
recipe.method: pdspy MCMC fit in visibility space of an exponentially tapered, hydrostatic, vertically isothermal flared disk (15 free parameters) with RADMC-3D models, galario for Fourier transform and emcee sampler
key_parameters: 200 walkers; minimum burn-in 1000 steps; convergence evaluated from 2500 steps
Position offsets restricted to initial imfit guess +-0.25 arcsec; V_LSR +-1.2 km/s (+-2.4 km/s for low S/N)
Temperature exponent q range expanded from [0,1] to [0,2] for sources piling up at q = 1
assumptions: Fixed CO/H2 = 1e-4 and 13CO/H2 = 10^-5.3; mean molecular weight 2.37; hydrostatic equilibrium; vertically isothermal disk
Pure Keplerian rotation (with pressure effects through the flared model); the CO traces disk gas, not outflows

recipe.goal: Choose best-fit values and uncertainties from the chains
recipe.method: Report the minimum-chi^2 fit with uncertainties from the min/max parameter values within Delta chi^2 = 15.975 over the last 1000 steps, instead of median and standard deviation

recipe.goal: Derive isochronal masses from five evolutionary model sets
recipe.method: Draw normal distributions in L* and Teff, interpolate through each track set with pdspy.stars, and take the median and scaled MAD of the mass distribution
key_parameters: Model sets: BHAC15, PARSEC v1.1, PARSEC v1.2S, Feiden (2016) non-magnetic and magnetic

recipe.method: Orthogonal distance regression of M_iso vs M_dyn, mass-ratio statistics, Spearman correlation of ratio with M_dyn, and two-sample KS tests, for the full sample and for M_dyn <= 1 Msun
key_parameters: Significance threshold p < 6.3e-5 (4 sigma) for Spearman correlation
Mass-limited sample M_dyn <= 1.0 Msun (excludes five sources)

recipe.goal: Derive disk dust masses and the Mdust-Mstar relation
recipe.method: Optically thin dust mass from the 870 um flux density, Gaia distance, opacity and dust temperature; ODR fit of log(Mdisk) vs log(Mstar) for dynamical and BHAC15 masses
key_parameters: kappa = 2.7 cm^2/g at 345 GHz; T_dust = 20 K or 25 K (L*/Lsun)^0.25
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission at 870 um with the stated opacity and the two T_dust prescriptions (gas-to-dust ratio not applied; dust masses only)

recipe.goal: Test for bias from binaries and inclination
recipe.method: Recompute all statistics without the five known or candidate binaries; compare M* and i with Barenfeld et al. 2017 using Spearman, medians and KS tests

score_reason: Project code, pdspy settings, priors, ranges, walkers, burn-in, convergence rule and statistical tests are given and numeric results are tabulated, but CASA/pdspy versions, imaging scripts, uv-data preparation and per-source adjustments are missing, and a full MCMC rerun of 23 radiative-transfer fits is expensive.
rediscovery_reason: Data come from a Cycle 7 program (2019.1.00493.S), the code is open and the recipe and numeric masses are tabulated; a reproducer could redo a handful of well-behaved sources, though full reproduction is compute-heavy and some per-source settings are not stated.
